title: vercel-labs/agent-desktop: a CLI that lets an agent operate desktop apps by name, not by pixel
friendlyTitle: vercel-labs/agent-desktop: a command-line tool that lets an agent use desktop apps by name, not by pixel
summary: Vercel Labs' agent-desktop is a command-line tool and C library for macOS, Windows, and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a reference for each element an agent can act on. The agent acts on that reference and snapshots again. It does not match pixels. Actions through the accessibility tree are headless by default, so they do not move the pointer or take focus unless you ask. Apache-2.0. friendlySummary: Vercel Labs' agent-desktop is a command-line tool and a C library for macOS, Windows, and Linux. A snapshot returns a JSON list, with a name for each thing on screen an agent can act on. The agent acts on that name and takes another snapshot. It does not guess from pixels. By default it uses the system's accessibility tools, so it does not move the mouse or steal focus unless you ask. The license is Apache-2.0. GitHub's daily trending list showed 2,243 stars today, and about 9,100 in total.
whyItMatters: Use it when an agent has to click, type, or read a desktop app, and you want a named element instead of a screenshot guess. On macOS you grant Accessibility permission. On Linux it needs the user's graphical session. Snapshots, clipboard reads, and screenshots can contain whatever is on the screen, so they do not belong in a public log.
